description: Custom Kubernetes controller that can be used to replicate secrets, configmaps and certificates.

summary.one_liner: Reflector is a Kubernetes controller that mirrors Secrets and ConfigMaps (including cert-manager certificate secrets) from a source object into other namespaces and keeps the copies in sync.
summary.what_it_does: Reflector watches Secrets and ConfigMaps for changes and copies their data into mirror objects in the same or other namespaces. A source object opts in with annotations that control which namespaces may reflect from it, by namespace name patterns or label selectors. A mirror points to its source with a "namespace/name" annotation. Reflector can also create mirrors automatically in matching namespaces, using the same name, and it deletes automatic mirrors when the source is removed or the namespace no longer matches. For Secrets it copies `data`; for ConfigMaps it copies `data` and `binaryData`. The README also shows how to annotate cert-manager Certificate and Ingress resources so the secrets they generate get mirrored. It is deployed with a Helm chart or a manual reflector.yaml manifest, and the README includes a Helm values table covering logging, watcher timeout, excluded namespaces, and TLS verification.
use_cases: Copy a wildcard TLS certificate secret into every namespace
Share a configmap across multiple Kubernetes namespaces
Mirror cert-manager certificate secrets to other namespaces
Automatically create secret copies in new namespaces
Restrict which namespaces may read a given secret by label selector
how_to_run: kubectl -n kube-system apply -f reflector.yaml (manual deployment file from the GitHub Releases page)
notable: Namespace allow-lists support glob-like patterns and label selectors, and a namespace matches if either condition is met
Automatic mirror creation with namespace filtering; automatic mirrors are removed when the source or permission is removed
Integrates with cert-manager via secretTemplate on Certificate and the cert-manager.io/secret-template annotation on Ingress
Multi-architecture images for amd64, arm and arm64
Documents a fix for FIPS-enabled nodes using OPENSSL_FORCE_FIPS_MODE=0
caveats: Requires Kubernetes 1.22+ and Helm 3.8+ if deployed with Helm
On FIPS-mode nodes the image crashes unless OPENSSL_FORCE_FIPS_MODE=0 is set, and that setting is not FIPS-validated
Conflicting resources with the same name in a target namespace are skipped for auto-mirroring and logged as warnings
